content.text:
Every service under services/ states some of its values and inherits the rest from platform/defaults.yaml.

For each policy, report how many services use it, how many of those are disabled, and the highest effective CPU limit among its enabled services. Then report how many services inherit their CPU limit, and the five services with the lowest effective CPU limit.

Answer as exactly these lines, policies alphabetically by name, and nothing else:

policy=<name> services=<n> disabled=<n> maxCpu=<value>
inherited=<n>
lowest=<service>:<limit>,<service>:<limit>,<service>:<limit>,<service>:<limit>,<service>:<limit>

policy=bronze services=40 disabled=3 maxCpu=4000m
policy=gold services=40 disabled=2 maxCpu=1000m
policy=silver services=40 disabled=2 maxCpu=2000m
inherited=24
lowest=billing-exporter:100m,catalog-indexer:100m,catalog-proxy:100m,checkout-scheduler:100m,identity-exporter:100m

Now add the disabled services, keeping every earlier line exactly as it was:

policy=<name> services=<n> disabled=<n> maxCpu=<value>
inherited=<n>
lowest=<service>:<limit>,<service>:<limit>,<service>:<limit>,<service>:<limit>,<service>:<limit>
disabled=<service>,<service>,...

Disabled services alphabetically by name. Nothing else.

policy=bronze services=40 disabled=3 maxCpu=4000m
policy=gold services=40 disabled=2 maxCpu=1000m
policy=silver services=40 disabled=2 maxCpu=2000m
inherited=24
lowest=billing-exporter:250m,catalog-indexer:100m,catalog-proxy:100m,checkout-scheduler:100m,identity-exporter:100m
disabled=billing-reconciler,checkout-indexer,identity-sync,ledger-exporter,orders-gateway,search-api,shipping-importer
